original.target_description: Manuscript p. 7 §7 Method chains and comments: overall perceived readability R1 for MC versus NoMC across all snippets.

n.sample_role: Snippet-level subject responses/observations across five snippets from 104 distinct participants; repeated observations, not 520 independent participants.
n.exclusions: 255 started; 110 completed; six completers excluded for extremely short code-reading and question-answering times. Final 104 participants supplied 520 observations. Three participants declaring a reading disorder were retained because their data were not outliers. No additional target-specific exclusions reported.

notes: Identity verified from canonical text: accepted peer-reviewed primary experimental report, matching title The Role of Method Chains and Comments in Software Readability and Comprehension – An Experiment, authors Jürgen Börstler and Barbara Paech, DOI 10.1109/TSE.2016.2527791. Full methods/results/appendices, manuscript pp. 1–17 after repository cover. Final journal pagination differs. No PDF supplied; no rendering. Only unfinished fields examined; other fields/sides are placeholders. §7 specifies chi-square tests for perceived-readability differences, but overall MC versus NoMC is only described as non-significant, without numeric chi-square, p or same-test p bound. Fig. 6 caption identifies counts/descriptive means, not test statistics. §§7.1–7.2 discuss experience groups/individual snippets and supply no numeric overall MC readability test. Adjacent χ2 = 16.1; α = 0.003 concerns comments and is excluded. Directly printed 520 observations from 104 participants; no inferred p threshold or N from df.
